speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Firms will increasingly face the need to relook at how they operate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Business models that once worked well may no longer be viable under the current and future environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In response, firms may need to pursue different pathways, transforming their business models, restructuring their operations or, where necessary, scale down or even exit specific products, services or parts of their operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our next thrust is therefore to support our businesses to proactively and confidently navigate these transitions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Such adjustments are a normal and necessary part of economic renewal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we recognise that the process can be difficult, challenging and sometimes, painful.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will work closely with trade associations and chambers, enterprises and the Labour Movement to support firms as they go through these transitions, helping them assess their options early, restructure responsibly, pursue new growth opportunities, including exploring overseas markets and manage change in a way that strengthens long-term competitiveness and supports workers through the transition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Mr Shawn Loh that with our small domestic economy, many growth opportunities lie beyond Singapore's shores.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We want to help our companies to not only export their products and services, but also to expand and invest internationally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition to growing their revenue and profits from overseas, these companies will bring value back to Singapore through better jobs, stronger demand for local capabilities and deeper integration into global growth opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Ms Elysa Chen and Mr Victor Lye on the importance of supporting and preparing our entrepreneurs and workers embarking on internationalisation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Ministry of Manpower will share more on this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also safeguard and expand our international economic space.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister of State Ms Gan Siow Hwang will elaborate more on our plans to deepen and diversify our economic links with our trading partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Chairman, the global environment will remain uncertain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But Singapore has succeeded so far not by waiting for certainty, but by planning long term, acting early and moving ahead decisively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The ESR has outlined our strategy going forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our five strategic thrusts build on our strengths, embrace new opportunities, harness technology, keep Singapore open and connected and support our people through change, every step of the way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will ensure growth must translate into good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Above all, our strategy is to give workers the confidence to adapt, businesses the ability to compete and every Singaporean a share in our progress and a stake in our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we continue to stay united, remain agile and nimble and keep investing in our people, Singapore will not just navigate change – we will shape it.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: Chairman, I declare my interest as a business owner that manufactures, assembles and distributes batteries locally.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: But I rise to speak about batteries not just as a product, but as an enabler for economic growth.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: Singapore may not manufacture battery cells at scale, but that is not where our competitive advantage lies.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: Our strengths and high value segments, such as system design, integration, battery management software, safety engineering, testing, compliance and project management.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: These are areas where our Singapore-based companies can compete and differentiate themselves.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: Today, many local companies are already working with IHLs and research institutes for technology capabilities, while leveraging regional manufacturing to produce competitive solutions.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: With the right positioning and partnerships, we can serve Southeast Asia and beyond.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: A handful of firms have shared that while they carry out substantial work in Singapore, including system integration, battery management software, safety engineering on compliance, this value-add may not always be fully reflected for trade purposes.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: I hope MTI can review whether our frameworks adequately recognise modern system integration and software-driven value-add in sectors like energy storage.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: Batteries enable solar deployment, power data centres, electrified fleets and strengthen grid resilience.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: With the right policy support, Singapore can capture meaningful value in this growing sector.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Chairman, secure energy and we secure our destiny.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Beyond meeting Singapore's basic needs, our energy demand will rise as we digitalise and double down on AI.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Singapore's energy strategy has always been shaped by three structural realities: we have no natural resources, we face land constraints and we depend almost entirely on imported energy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: These constraints constantly force us to balance the energy trilemma – security, sustainability and affordability.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It remains our most viable transition fuel, reliable and relatively lower in emissions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We have diversified supplies through pipeline gas and LNG imports and invested in critical infrastructure, such as our LNG terminal.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: At the same time, we are accelerating decarbonisation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I welcome continued efforts to maximise solar deployment on rooftops and reservoirs, pilot regional electricity imports under the ASEAN Power Grid initiative and study hydrogen as a potential long‑term option.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Yet, our strategy must continue to evolve in the face of rising geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain fragmentation and intensifying climate pressures.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The latest conflict involving Israel, US and Iran is a stark example.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I therefore pose several questions to the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: As we deepen regional electricity imports, how is MTI assessing geopolitical concentration and supply risk?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: What plans are in place to diversify sources and build redundancy into our long-term energy import strategy?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: With rising demand for computing power and data centres, how is MTI working with local and international partners to ensure sufficient, sustainable power supply while promoting energy efficient digital infrastructure?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Hydrogen is promising for low carbon power and for hard to abate sectors, such as maritime and petrochemicals.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: When does the Ministry assess hydrogen to be commercially viable at scale for Singapore?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How are we positioning ourselves early enough to shape, rather than follow, regional hydrogen supply chains?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: What support is being offered to firms and startups to deepen R&D and commercialise hydrogen technologies in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How does MTI balance competitiveness for trade exposed sectors with the need for credible carbon pricing?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Are there plans to deepen international carbon market linkages or other measures to manage domestic cost pressures?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How will the Ministry ensure households and businesses continue to access reliable energy at affordable prices during this transition?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Energy policy today is not just about keeping the lights on.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is about resilience in a fractured world and competitiveness in a low-carbon economy.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Mr Chairman, I rise to speak on electricity, because in today’s AI-driven economy, energy is a strategic capability.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Earlier this month, I asked about Singapore's energy resilience and grid stability as renewable deployment grows and electrification accelerates.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: We are pursuing decarbonisation and digitalisation simultaneously and our electricity system must support both without compromising reliability or affordability.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: How do we keep Singapore's transition to low-carbon electricity credible despite price volatility?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Investors need certainty, yet committed off-take arrangements may raise costs relative to market prices.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: How do we balance investment certainty with affordability?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Clear policy signals will be critical to sustain private capital.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Intermittency now exists on both supply and demand.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Electrified transport and fast-charging infrastructure will create concentrated demand peaks.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: For sectors such as data centres and semiconductors, energy reliability is non-negotiable.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Electricity pricing does not always reflect supply variability.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Could more dynamic pricing better align demand with peak renewable generation?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Regulatory frameworks should also continue enabling private investment in renewable generation and energy storage.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Mr Chairman, energy resilience, affordability and decarbonisation are the foundations of national competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Chairman, as the Deputy Prime Minister has highlighted, the rules that allowed Singapore to prosper have fundamentally changed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Climate change continues to accelerate, and its impact is affecting our way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: How do we therefore seize opportunities in spite of all these challenges?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will leverage science and technology to establish leadership in key growth sectors and push the frontier into new growth areas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also strive to establish Singapore as an AI leader, transforming our advanced manufacturing industry.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Powering these efforts, at the core, is energy, which must be sustainable, secure, reliable and affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To extend our lead in advanced manufacturing, we will continue to direct national-level R&D resources towards our key growth sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 investments have boosted the R&D capability and capacity of our economy as well as created good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Industry R&D jobs grew by 36% between 2016 and 2023 to more than 30,000, of which more than 70% were filled by locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Flagship will translate research into products and encourage more advanced R&D and manufacturing activities, creating good jobs in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Flagship will also bring together efforts under the National Semiconductor Translation and Innovation Centre (NSTIC).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since its launch in RIE2025, NSTIC has achieved several breakthroughs, including in high-speed data transmission and metalens fabrication.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It has since attracted over 10 industry partners and has built a strong commercialisation pipeline.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, the Deputy Prime Minister announced our investment in NSTIC (R&D Fab), which is our semiconductor R&D fabrication facility.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Within a year, we aim to double the carrier mobility of silicon carbide technologies, enabling the potential development of smaller, but more efficient power systems.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Use cases include extending the driving ranges of electric vehicles (EVs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Another key growth sector is biomedical, which remains robust despite its inherent volatility.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To boost sector growth, we announced two R&D translational platforms in 2024, namely the Nucleic Acid Therapeutics Initiative (NATi) and MedTech Catapult.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These platforms are attracting global partners, they are uplifting local enterprises, and training talents to anchor high-value R&D activities and jobs in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, MedTech Catapult is working with a local startup, Vivo Surgical, to develop its verification prototype to be ready for clinical studies, and has onboarded the company onto its venture acceleration programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Given the good progress of these platforms, we intend to scale them further under RIE2030.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides public sector efforts, the private sector also plays a crucial role in our innovation ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through our Research and Innovation Scheme for Companies (RIS(C)), we have attracted substantive private research and innovation investments, building capabilities and creating high-value jobs for locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the past five years, companies have committed more than $14 billion to research and innovation investments here; and it has created more than 12,000 jobs in research, development, and innovation roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Again, with locals filling more than 70% of these positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Grab's Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence has hired around 50 people, while Evonik, the German chemicals giant, has hired over 100 researchers for its Asia Research Hub in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond existing growth sectors, we will boldly pursue emerging technologies that can drive breakthroughs across our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One example is space technology, the “final frontier”, which is rapidly moving from science fiction to real-world applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Space technology is already used in our daily lives, powering navigation and connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As technologies advance, as costs fall, smaller countries like Singapore can capture opportunities in the growing space economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This can create good jobs for Singaporeans in areas such as engineering and data science, while enabling businesses to capture value from space-enabled services and applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One such opportunity is space-based Earth observation, which can be used in industries such as maritime, sustainability and finance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A local startup, Arkadiah Technology, is using satellite data in its partnership with a global agribusiness company – Golden Agri-Resources – to support digital measurement, reporting and verification.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This enables more accurate carbon accounting of tropical forests.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To advance our ambitions, we will be establishing the National Space Agency of Singapore (NSAS), which I announced last month.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we develop our growth sectors, we will continue to partner firms to equip Singaporeans with in-demand and emerging skills.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Earlier, the Deputy Prime Minister shared our vision to establish Singapore as an AI leader, with an AI-empowered economy, through the development and execution of AI Missions across four priority sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will work with industry partners to further develop the AI Missions and we will provide an update later.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These preliminarily will be anchored on three thrusts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, we will leverage AI and robotics to transform our manufacturing facilities to achieve best-in-class outcomes that can become more agile, more resilient and more efficient.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, we will harness AI to create first-in-the-world solutions, by enhancing product designs and accelerating development cycles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, we will drive broad-based sectoral transformation, by helping companies adopt AI in key operations to accelerate the deployment of solutions across the ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To support these efforts, we will strengthen two key enablers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, A*STAR's Sectoral AI Centre of Excellence in Manufacturing (AIMfg).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, Sunningdale, which is a large local manufacturer of precision-engineered plastic components, is partnering AIMfg to develop an AI-powered defect detection system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: AIMfg has also developed a set of common AI models that address typical business needs, such as a predictive maintenance model for rotary devices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This reduces resources and time needed to develop custom solutions from scratch.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Moving forward, AIMfg will further drive AI-led transformation with partners and expand the suite of common AI models.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, we will build capabilities in Embodied AI.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Embodied AI brings AI into our physical world – robots that can sense their surroundings, that can reason independently and they can act with purpose in unfamiliar environments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will invest in R&D to address complex problems faced by our companies and provide shared infrastructure for researchers and companies to test new Embodied AI technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Such infrastructure can accelerate deployment of technologies in frontier sectors, which is something that Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will begin with the Advanced Manufacturing, Aviation and Maritime sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This can seed new growth areas, by attracting next-generation Embodied AI startups as well as grooming local champions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To fully unlock AI’s potential for businesses, we will also contemporaneously build an AI-ready workforce through education and training, and support companies in job redesign and workforce transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will elaborate on these efforts in my Ministry of Manpower speech tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Chairman, given these shifts, our economy is becoming more digital and innovation-driven.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As pointed out by Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Edward Chia, energy powers all these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For our economy and our way of life, energy is existential.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As demand grows and as we decarbonise, the Government will continue to strike a pragmatic balance between energy sustainability, security and affordability.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Decarbonisation will come with costs, but it cannot and it will not be at all costs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will regularly review the transitory allowances, which only cover a portion of companies’ emissions, for us to strike the right balance between maintaining a price signal to encourage investments in low-carbon solutions and managing the rising costs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we pursue a diversified portfolio of renewable energy pathways, we will also focus on scalable and cost-effective solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As with Singapore’s Water Story, we will first prioritise pathways that support our self-sufficiency and resilience, by maximising our indigenous sources.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Solar remains our most viable option in the near term.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, even with widespread deployment, solar will only supply, at best, about 10% of our future electricity needs, due to land constraints and climate conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, while solar energy is important, it is insufficient.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: That is why we are currently studying our geothermal resource potential.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides indigenous sources, we are also pursuing other low-carbon pathways.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Electricity imports from the region can diversify and decarbonise our energy mix.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To date, we have awarded around 8.4 gigawatts (GW) of Conditional Approvals to promising projects.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Of which, three GW have advanced to Conditional Licences.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are working closely with project developers to secure the necessary regulatory approvals to commence construction soon.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through close collaboration and cooperation with our neighbours, which is essential, as we strive towards our regional vision of the ASEAN power grid, our first wave of electricity import projects will likely come from Indonesia and Peninsular Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond this, we are also exploring other low-carbon solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As I have said before in this House, no option is off the table.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Its compatibility with existing infrastructure minimises the need for costly asset upgrades.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since last year, we have seen strong industry interest.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are currently evaluating proposals for the sandbox, and we expect to appoint demand-supply aggregators soon.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, we are studying the potential of low-carbon hydrogen, including its derivatives, or its carriers, such as ammonia.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last October, we appointed a consortium led by Keppel to conduct Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) studies for the next phase of the ammonia pilot project for power generation and bunkering.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, we are also studying the potential of carbon capture, utilisation and storage solutions to decarbonise hard-to-abate sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue working with countries that have suitable geological sites for carbon storage, such as Australia, Indonesia and Malaysia, on bilateral agreements to offer the private sector greater investment certainty.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also studying ways to store captured carbon permanently in products such as building materials.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Based on the results, we will assess how these pathways can be scaled up, the type of mix possible, to achieve our decarbonisation ambitions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even as we pursue all of these options, we must remain clear-eyed about their inherent challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Imported electricity comes with significant geopolitical risks and uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Other low-carbon solutions are not yet ready for deployment at scale, either due to technological nascency or under-developed supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Thus, while we have not made a decision – and let me reiterate this, we have not made a decision – we are seriously studying the potential deployment of advanced nuclear energy technologies, such as small modular reactors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nuclear energy has the potential to be a safe, reliable and cost-competitive option.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Its high fuel density is especially attractive for land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Five one-inch-tall pellets, which are each smaller than my thumb, can generate the same amount of energy as one Olympic-sized swimming pool of natural gas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are intensifying our capability building, especially in nuclear safety and technology assessment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will do so in line with the International Atomic Energy Agency's Milestones Approach, and we will partner international leaders such as the US, France and the Republic of Korea.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, just this morning, this is one of the few moments I come in with a tie, this morning, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) just signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power Company, which operates South Korea's entire fleet of 26 nuclear energy reactors, on the sidelines of the President's visit from the Republic of Korea.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will work closely with partners on raising awareness, not just for nuclear, but more fundamentally, the existential nature of energy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Mr Edward Chia and Mr Ng Shi Xuan have pointed out, we must continue to ensure the continued reliability of the grid, as Singapore moves to a heterogeneous mix of energy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, EMA and SP Group launched the Future Grid Capabilities Roadmap to set clear directions for capability building in areas, such as system inertia and flexibility technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA is also piloting a Virtual Power Plant regulatory sandbox with industry partners and assessing whether more energy storage systems are required, to address challenges such as intermittency.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Building on past efforts, we are significantly increasing investments in promising solutions to reduce power sector and industry emissions and, at the same time, to ensure a reliable and resilient power system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Under this Grand Challenge, we are launching a new programme, Singapore Pilots for Energy and Enterprise Decarbonisation (SPEED).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Speeding is an offence for the Land Transport Authority.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This supports local translational Research, Development and Demonstration activities and it catalyses private investments, to scale up promising yet nascent technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Chairman, innovation and technology will continue to push and propel Singapore to greater heights, and it will create good jobs for generations to come.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Deputy Prime Minister pointed out earlier, we are a climate realist.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we strive towards our net-zero ambition, we have to constantly remain mindful of the challenges, such as the geographical constraints and rising decarbonisation costs to businesses and households.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But that said, we will do our utmost best to secure a clean and green future, because this is for our future generations, with a stable and reliable flow of energy, which is existential for our economy and our way of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong spoke about how Singapore is now entering a new phase in our economic journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are committed to empowering businesses to succeed and thrive in this new landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to nurture a dynamic and vibrant enterprise ecosystem, where enterprises confidently navigate change and succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses today face increasing pressure to adapt in an uncertain world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have gained keen insights from our engagements with SMEs and the trade associations and chambers (TACs), including the Singapore Business Federation about the challenges on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Several Members have raised similar concerns, particularly in relation to our SMEs – Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Mark Lee, Mr Lee Hong Chuang, Mr Shawn Loh, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Ng Shi Xuan and Ms Denise Phua.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also enable our businesses to proactively navigate transitions, while continuing to strengthen our consumer protection framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the years, the Government has rolled out a range of schemes to support companies in capability building, productivity and efficiency improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses that can do more with less and respond quickly to changes are best positioned to stay competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Structural changes brought about by AI and decarbonisation will mean that businesses have to adapt to stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: But these changes also present opportunities for businesses to transform and to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Ng Shi Xuan and Ms Denise Phua that we will continue to enable and empower enterprises across all sectors to optimise production processes and to reduce business costs, especially through technology and automation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, enterprises with warehousing operations are increasingly adopting automated logistics solutions to enhance operational efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They can tap on schemes, such as the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) for funds, and advisory support from industry partners, like the Republic Polytechnic's Centre of Innovation for Supply Chain Management (COI-SCM).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One quick example is the company Frosts Food & Beverage, which operates facilities totalling 75,000 square feet in Bedok and Tuas for the storage and distribution of food products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Beyond productivity improvements, we are continuing to help our enterprises move towards a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have heard from Minister Tan See Leng earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will facilitate continued access to financing for companies seeking to build green capabilities and capture new opportunities in the green economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, to help companies manage rising energy costs and reduce their environmental footprint, we will extend the Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) for one year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will provide continued support for investments in energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The second thrust of our package helps the businesses grow revenue by capturing opportunities at home and abroad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will help our businesses seize opportunities from the shifting international business environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Mr Shawn Loh that we will continue to strengthen access to financing through schemes like the EFS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, launched in 2019, the EFS has supported thousands of enterprises in securing financing for a wide range of business activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will enhance the EFS in two ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This means that our enterprises can obtain loan facilities that best meet their needs, whether is it fulfilling their contracts, executing projects, or undertaking capital investments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we will permanently expand the scope of the EFS-Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) to support companies in securing financing for both domestic and overseas acquisitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As global supply chains reconfigure and our domestic market matures, our enterprises are increasingly looking to seize opportunities beyond our shores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our approach has always been to lower the barriers to entry, to strengthen access to markets and to provide calibrated support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, like what Members have said, we recognise that expanding businesses overseas now comes with increased risks and uncertainty, like what Mr Mark Lee has mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Mark Lee and Mr Azhar Othman will be glad to hear that we are indeed stepping up our efforts to help our businesses as they embark on their internationalisation journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This includes schemes like the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) grant, the Business Adaptation Grant and the Global Innovation Alliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we will further enhance the MRA grant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I think this is a point that Mr Shawn Loh will appreciate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will not only support businesses in accessing new markets but also enable them to deepen their presence in existing markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Next, we will enhance the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation (DTDi) scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Lastly, the Global Innovation Alliance will have a refreshed strategy which supports startups' market expansion across two tracks, "Launch" and "Grow".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Startups new to the market will be supported through "Launch" programmes focused on market discovery and familiarisation, shorter market sprints and early customer and partner discovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Startups and SMEs requiring more tailored support can tap on "Grow" pathways to access specialised partnerships to support expansion, deeper market penetration and accelerate technology maturation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, no discussion of our enterprises will be complete without mentioning our heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Heartland shops intersect closely with the lives of everyday Singaporeans, contributing to the character and the vibrancy of our communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Helping our heartland enterprises also entails enabling their adaptation and renewal for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the years, the Government has supported heartland enterprises in refreshing their product offerings, adopting novel concepts and creating experiences that draw footfall and in fact, increasingly, online orders as well, and also strengthening community ties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage our heartland shops to take this opportunity to refresh their stores and conceive exciting placemaking activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of our heartland shops are small and micro enterprises, which, as Mr Gerald Giam has mentioned earlier, play a fundamental role in the local economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government certainly recognise the unique challenges faced by firms of different sizes, including micro-SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have developed targeted assistance to address specific needs and support their long-term growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, enterprises in sectors with high concentrations of micro-SMEs, such as F&B and Personal Services, are benefiting from sector-specific support to tackle operational challenges, raise productivity and thereby, improving their top line and bottom line.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand, many of the F&B establishment face structural cost pressures and capability gaps, as mentioned by some of the Members, including Ms Denise Phua, earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And this was also indicated in the recently launched Food Services Productivity Report commissioned by Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Productivity Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This, in turn, leads to compressed margins and limited ability to scale sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, the same report also revealed that the top F&B performers were able to generate close to three times more sales per man-hour, compared to those at the bottom.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: When we look closely at it, the top performing F&B establishments observed five key practices: number one, generally, they embraced and adopted digitalisation and automation; number two, implemented strategic menu design; number three, streamlined workflows and space layouts; number four, outsourced labour-intensive preparation work; and number five, adopted effective workforce management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, MTI and Enterprise Singapore will continue to do our utmost to enable and to equip our F&B establishments to gain these critical capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To help our businesses adopt such best practices, during the Food Services Forum held months ago, we launched three new initiatives to support the food sector to: one, optimise operations through the F&B Process Optimisation programme (POP); two, to strengthen their supply chains through the FoodX Programme, which then supports the F&B companies in centralising their food preparation; three, to accelerate the digital transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides all these sector-specific schemes, micro-SMEs looking to build their core capabilities and scale up can also tap on schemes, such as the EDG and Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG), for customised support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, we encourage them to approach any of our 10 SME Centres for tailored advice and guidance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, underpinning our efforts to help businesses enhance productivity and efficiency and grow is a pro-enterprise and trusted business environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is the focus of the third thrust of the Business Refresh Package.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will simplify the grant application process by combining Enterprise Singapore's three flagship grants, and businesses will find it easier to navigate and apply for funding as they only need to submit a single application under the combined grant framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses that require more support for customised projects can certainly continue to apply to Enterprise Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses will always have the flexibility to embark on projects aligned to their specific needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And once launched, the enhancements to the MRA grant that I just mentioned earlier will come under EDGE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, last year, the Government set up the Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Pro-Enterprise Office (SME PEO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The SME PEO supports businesses by addressing regulatory feedback that spans multiple public agencies, as well as issues arising in new or emerging sectors where regulations may be unclear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Building on the work of the Alliance for Action on Business Competitiveness in 2024, we also announced three Statements of Commitments under the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review, to enhance regulatory agility and to reduce compliance burden for businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The SME PEO has been working with agencies to implement these commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This helps make our processes more transparent and predictable for businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, to extend the validity of business licences to at least three years, and up to five years where we can.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, 45% of all business licences have a validity period of at least three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And in three years' time, by 2029, this will increase to 80%, with agencies actively reviewing their policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Lastly, to streamline processes to reduce sequential approvals and repeated requests for information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have simplified multi-agency processes to shorten administrative timelines and to reduce back-and-forth with approving authorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, companies required to undergo Quantitative Risk Assessments (QRA) are expected to save more than 40 days per application following the streamlining of processes by the relevant agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also continue to work with agencies to simplify internal processes across domains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One such area is the industrial lease assignments or the transfer of industrial land sites in the secondary market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Currently, all assignment applications are subject to JTC's comprehensive assessment of the buyer's business plan and economic contributions, regardless of the land area or the remaining tenure of the site.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Moving forward, the assignment assessment process will be streamlined for small sites of up to 1.5 hectares, with short remaining lease tenure of no more than 15 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The proposed uses must support manufacturing activities and there must also be sufficient infrastructure capacity at the sites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: JTC will exempt these cases from the full assessment process and will only carry out requisite checks to ensure that assignees comply with prevailing policy and land use guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The revised workflow could reduce the processing time for eligible assignment applications to within one month from the date of the full application.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: JTC will release more details on this initiative in the first half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Even as we support firms in pursuing their growth ambition and simplify the processes, we must be prepared to proactively navigate transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Companies shared that with the ESR that understanding their business health and future options were vital in navigating transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong highlighted, businesses will need to adapt to shifting global trade flows, technological disruptions and in fact, tighter resource constraints amid steep changes in the global landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This may entail reinventing operating models, as Mr Edward Chia has mentioned earlier, for family and heritage businesses, managing generational transitions to safeguard their legacies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses can reposition and transform by moving into higher value-added activities, optimising operations, offshoring where appropriate or pivoting towards more viable opportunities to redeploy resources more productively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The creation, the growth and the consolidation of businesses are all part of a very healthy, vibrant and dynamic enterprise ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will journey with our companies every step of the way as they navigate transitions and be their support to help them adapt and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The ESR Committee will share more details in time to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, our trusted business environment is underpinned by consumers' confidence in our businesses and market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Andre Low on the need for robust deterrence and enforcement against unfair trade practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCS) has stepped up its enforcement efforts and secured undertakings from businesses to cease unfair practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, such actions require careful investigation and due legal process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On Mr Andre Low's suggestion to strengthen deterrence against egregious companies, we would like to assure you that the Government is monitoring this very closely and stands prepared to take on a whole-of-Government view to enhance our consumer protection regime to safeguard the emerging risks as well as the need to give our enforcement agencies more teeth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Panel will submit its findings to the Government later this year for a thorough review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, the years ahead will be defined by the steps we take today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through our efforts to raise productivity, support growth and internationalisation, as well as to foster a pro-enterprise environment, we are laying the groundwork for a more resilient, dynamic and competitive enterprise ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: By working closely with our businesses and trade associations, we will build new capabilities that allow our businesses to respond decisively to uncertainty and to seize opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With these foundations in place, we are confident that our enterprises will not only weather the uncertainty ahead, but continue to grow with strength, resilience and purpose to adapt, transform and succeed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling spoke of how we are helping businesses weather uncertainty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To do so, we must stay relevant in two ways: first, remain attractive to visitors; second, build a vibrant startup ecosystem that is attractive to founders, here and beyond.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Let us start with how we are making Singapore more attractive to visitors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked for updates on Tourism 2040.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Tourism 2040 is our long-term roadmap that is anchored on quality tourism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are expanding our reach in segments and markets that can drive higher tourism returns and working with our industry to create more exciting and distinctive experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There are a few reasons for this good performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, we continued to deliver world-class events, including concerts by Lady Gaga and the World Aquatics Championships 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also hosted major meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) events and opened major attractions, such as Rainforest Wild and Illumination's Minion Land.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To remain attractive to visitors, we will strengthen our stage, our people and our show.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: One of our key tourism precincts is Sentosa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2019, then-Prime Minister Lee talked about building the Greater Southern Waterfront, including developing Pulau Brani together with Sentosa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I am pleased to update that we have commenced the first phase of our Greater Sentosa Master Plan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In Phase One, we will upgrade Sentosa's infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will add a new transport hub to link Sentosa and Brani, which are collectively known as Greater Sentosa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will also house lifestyle and hospitality developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also plan to replace the Sentosa Express to improve connectivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also rejuvenate our beaches and add coastal protection measures, so visitors can enjoy a day on the beach, even as we protect Sentosa from rising sea levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also create new icons in Sentosa, like Imbiah Canopy, which will become a beacon atop Mount Imbiah that leads visitors to heritage buildings and nature trails.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will share more details about our Greater Sentosa Master Plan later this year and I invite the public to share your ideas with us as we continue to reimagine and shape Greater Sentosa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I would also like to update Singaporeans on our progress to refresh Orchard Road.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The historic Emerald Hill will be part of this refresh.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will launch a tender in the coming months to transform 37 Emerald Hill, site of the former Singapore Chinese Girls' School.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will be a mixed-use development featuring unique hotel concepts, lifestyle offerings and community and public spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also on track to complete the Grange Road Event Space in the fourth quarter of 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The 3,000-capacity venue can host international touring acts and local artistes – bringing live music, community and cultural events right at the heart of Orchard Road.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also enhancing our cruise infrastructure and reinforcing our position as one of Asia's leading cruise hubs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This enables two large cruise ships to berth concurrently, allowing us to welcome more cruise lines, like Disney Adventure, which will call Singapore home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I look forward to attending the ship's christening this week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our tourism workers and businesses shape how every visitor experiences Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will continue to equip them with the tools to excel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, our Tourism Leadership Excellence and Advancement Programme equips tourism professionals with skills in both tech and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our tourism businesses have also been using AI and other tech, and we will help them better use these tools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) will unveil the Industry Digital Plans for the Travel Agents and MICE industries, alongside a GenAI Roadmap, at our upcoming Tourism Industry Conference in May.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We continue to be attractive to art lovers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In addition to kicking off Singapore Art Week 2026 in January, we have brought "Botero in Singapore" to Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Singapore is the first and only stop here in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like art fans, music fans have been attracted to Singapore over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, they will enjoy acts like BTS World Tour in December, made possible through STB's partnership with HYBE and Klook.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will be BTS' longest-running Asian stop outside of Korea and Japan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have also made Singapore an attractive e-sports destination over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, we will host PGL Major Singapore 2026, the first Counter-Strike 2 Major event in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year's F1 will also be different and more exciting, because we have secured our first ever F1 Sprint event.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This means that F1 teams will also compete for championship points on Saturday.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are one of only six circuits to host this in 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: F1 fans will know it will make our race weekend even more exciting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our MICE industry also continues to attract quality visitors and position ourselves to cement Singapore as a business destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will host major events this year such as the Passenger Terminal Expo Asia and the RECHARGE Wind Power Summit Asia Pacific.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will host many ASEAN events as chair next year, including the ASEAN Tourism Forum 2027.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is an important event for us to strengthen regional tourism cooperation and showcase Singapore to our neighbours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will next speak about how we are going to be attractive to startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our startup ecosystem has evolved significantly over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To date, we have over 4,500 tech startups, 220 incubators and 500 VC firms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As co-chair of the ESR Committee on Entrepreneurship, alongside Minister of State Dinesh Vasu Dash, we have engaged stakeholders across the startup ecosystem to develop recommendations to enhance their access to capital, markets and talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked how we can strengthen pathways beyond capital incentives so Singaporeans of all stages and all groups can venture into entrepreneurship and return to employment without being disadvantaged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are developing further measures under our committee and we welcome members of the public to share your ideas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our committee has been working on ideas to expand startups' access to capital, and I will share how we are doing so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will be to continue to invest into early-stage startups as well as expand into growth-stage deep tech startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, SSGE supports new and early-stage deep tech startups by co-investing with qualified private sector investors and investing in global VC firms that in turn invest in these startups through a fund-of-funds approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: One such fund is Matter Venture Partners, a Silicon Valley-based HardTech VC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Matter has invested in early-stage Singapore-based startups, encouraged its portfolio companies to have a strong business and R&D footprint in Singapore, and mentored local startup founders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SSGE also benefits early-stage deep tech companies like Blue Whale Energy (BWE), which builds and operates a Virtual Power Plant platform, combining its own sodium-ion batteries with edge-based control software to create a flexible energy network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SSGE funding can help BWE crowd in private capital and speed up its development for large-scale deployment in Singapore and expansion into other markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Ng Shi Xuan asked about the gap we are trying to close with the additional $1 billion injection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We now have maturing crop of high-potential deep tech startups like Nuevocor, a biotech firm that develops potential life-saving medicines for heart muscle diseases caused by genetic mutations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Nuevocor closed a US$45 million Series B funding round in May 2025 and will enter clinical trials across the US and Europe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Growth-stage deep tech startups like Nuevocor need substantial capital to scale beyond our early-stage support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we will directly invest in growth-stage deep tech startups like Nuevocor.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will provide them with the capital they need to scale their operations, strengthen their teams and enter new markets while remaining anchored in Singapore as their home base.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we will invest in global growth-stage deep tech VC funds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: By expanding our fund-of-funds approach, we will attract top-tier growth investors to establish their presence in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They will bring capital, global networks, expertise and deep experience in scaling frontier tech, helping to grow and expand our deep tech startups globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Third, we will continue co-investing with third-party investors into early-stage deep tech startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: By sharing risks with credible investors, we will catalyse private capital and strengthen market discipline for our early-stage startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Ng Shi Xuan asked if the Startup SG Founder programme only applies to first-time founders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In April 2024, we have made the programme more flexible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While the main applicant needs to be a first-time founder, they can now partner founders who have previous startup experiences to apply.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Neo Kok Beng pointed out that our startups receive great support during the seed stage but face difficulties as they start to mature, due to uncertainty of exit liquidity for investors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To address this, we are strengthening options for companies to raise capital in both public and private markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2022, we set up the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund to attract and anchor listings of high-growth companies, including promising startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like the first tranche, we will co-invest in Anchor Fund 2 with Temasek.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is the second move arising from our ESR Entrepreneurship Committee's work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will complement the new initiatives from the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') Equities Market Review Group, which has seen our equity market achieve some early wins with increased IPO activity and higher average daily trading volumes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our upcoming SGX-Nasdaq dual listing bridge will also allow eligible companies to simultaneously list on both exchanges with one set of prospectus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will open NASDAQ's new Singapore Office next week with NASDAQ's management and we look forward to working with the NASDAQ team in the run-up to the launch of the Global Listing Board.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, I have spoken of how we will continue to make Singapore more attractive to visitors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have also spoken about how we will continue to make us even more attractive to startups, to founders and to enterprises, by strengthening our startup ecosystem and helping innovative companies thrive and seek funds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will now handover to Minister of State Gan Siow Huang to speak about how we are addressing their need for space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister of State Alvin Tan has just spoken on how we can catalyse startup communities by availing capital to help them scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I will focus on how we provide physical space and critical infrastructure to support startups in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One-North by JTC is our main node for startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is a major knowledge and innovation district and it houses leading firms such as Grab, Razer, Sea and research institutions in A*STAR, the National University of Singapore (NUS), National University Hospital (NUH) and Singapore Science Park.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, it hosts over 30 incubators, accelerators and venture capital firms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Home-grown company Igloo is one such startup that LaunchPad has nurtured to success.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Beginning with smart lock solutions in 2016, it has scaled to enterprise-grade access control software for property and facilities management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It has expanded to eight countries, including the US and China, with about 80 global distributors and 90% of its revenue coming from abroad.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information announced recently that it is extending its AI co-working space, Lorong AI, at Cross Street to LaunchPad.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This follows recent engagements with the startup ecosystem, including venture capital funds and accelerators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The refresh will essentially boost the vibrant environment for startups to work, live and play.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will be Singapore's hub and home for AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It will be the first startup community in Singapore with work and living spaces under one roof.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Startups can house their researchers and developers here, leveraging the events, speakers and demos happening at the same place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Members may also access them through the MP@SG Parl app.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Deputy Prime Minister Gan had spoken earlier on establishing Singapore as an AI leader.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also suggested that our growth be supported by AI diffusion across sectors, among other productivity measures.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The other block will have 200 residential units.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It will be developed through repurposing blocks in the extended LaunchPad, within walking distance of One-North and Kent Ridge Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Moving on to another part of Singapore, JTC will be establishing a new LaunchPad at Punggol Digital District, completing it in phases from end of 2026.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As a smart district embedded within the community, Punggol Digital District (PDD) is the ideal testbed for translating innovations in smart city, robotics and cybersecurity sectors into real-world solutions.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It houses startups, industry, academia and the community under one roof.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The growing ecosystem of companies and agencies in PDD include UOB, OCBC, GovTech, Cybersecurity Agency of Singapore and Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT).

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Training providers, such as SITLEARN, SIT's Continuous Education Training centre, will have a front-row view of innovation development to incorporate these new skills into its adult learning curriculum.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Another key pillar is PDD's Open Digital Platform, which collects district data and allows lifelike simulations.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: JTC is working with the Infocomm Media Development Authority, GovTech and SIT to enhance the collection and sharing of the data.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The Open Digital Platform will link the innovations to PDD's infrastructure, such as gantries and lifts, to run real-world pilots.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For instance, if a robotics startup like dConstruct Robotics wants to deploy applications, such as autonomous delivery, their robots can navigate buildings to deliver parcels or food to users, bringing greater convenience to the PDD occupants.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Beyond catalysing groundbreaking developments here, our firms must seize opportunities regionally.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: ASEAN is projected to be the world's fourth-largest economic bloc by 2030 and we are building nodes including the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone and Batam Bintan Karimun.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The first phase is expected to complete around 2030.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Woodlands Gateway will offer commercial and lifestyle amenities for commuters, residents and people working in the Woodlands North area.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Given its proximity to the RTS Link, Woodlands Gateway will cater to firms siting manufacturing in Johor with their regional HQ functions in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Leading global precision optics supplier, Edmund Optics, demonstrates the benefits of this twinning model.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Its facility in Woodlands North Coast serves as a sales, innovation and R&D facility, whilst its Johor facility manufactures the components.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As a crucial node in Edmund Optics' global footprint, this twinned ecosystem has helped the firm remain cost-efficient and competitive while providing jobs to people in both countries.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The RTS Link will make this ecosystem connection even more seamless.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Mr Chairman, beyond providing quality industrial spaces, we must also safeguard and expand Singapore's international economic space.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: With total trade exceeding three times of our GDP, global connectivity creates real opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: However, we know that global trade is also fragmenting.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
